items.title: Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue
items.description: Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation’s five board directors if any of Manchester City ‘s sponsors sue them. The clubs met in London on Thursday for the first time since an independent commission found City guilty of a catalogue of charges relating to breaches of the league’s financial rules in September. City have appealed and maintain their innocence, with a sanction yet to be decided. The club’s sponsors Etihad and Etisalat have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League. At present, under the league’s articles of association, a director is financially covered if they win a legal case brought against them by a third party, but not if they lose. The league will update its rules to extend legal indemnity to chief executive Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittan and three other non-executive directors . City and Nottingham Forest were the only two clubs that voted against the proposal to provide extra legal protection, with the other 18 clubs voting in favour. Due to collective responsibility, it means that all clubs are now liable to cover legal costs that could run into hundreds of millions of pounds, raising the intriguing possibility of City being financially impacted by the legal action of its own sponsors. BBC Sport was told that City’s CFO Ingo Bank asked Premier League chair Brittan during Thursday’s meeting if the proposal was a direct result of threats of legal action from Etihad and Etisalat, but she said she could not comment. While Forest have declined to comment, their objection to the proposal is said have to been on procedural grounds, rather than due to any support for City. The club did not believe that sufficient information had been provided, or adequate time afforded, for clubs to properly consider the implications of the proposed amendment, particularly given the potentially significant financial responsibilities involved. It felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before clubs were asked to vote. An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City guilty of artificially inflating the club’s revenues by over £830m over a nine-year period in September. The commission determined that the club arranged “sham” contracts with sponsors, which disguised funding from club owners the Abu Dhabi United Group. Premier League CEO Masters said City “systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade”. In October, City sponsor Etihad Airways said it was considering legal action against the Premier League . In a statement, the United Arab Emirates-based airline said it “categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements”. Etisalat signalled its intention to follow suit earlier this month and described the Premier League’s verdict as “entirely false and defamatory”.

items.title: World Fisheries Day: Making Ghana’s expanded Inshore Exclusion Zone work for artisanal fishers
items.description: What good is a law that protects fishing communities if they do not know it exists, cannot tell when it is being broken, or do not know where to turn? For more than 22 years, Kwesi Atta has fished out of Ezilinbo, a coastal community in the Jomoro Municipality of the Western Region. The sea has fed his family and sustained his community. But making a living has become harder. Industrial trawlers compete with canoe fishers for the same grounds, and the tension sometimes turns into open confrontation at sea. What stands out in Kwesi’s experience is not only the competition but what he did not know. Neither he nor many of his fellow fishers were aware of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), or that it expands the Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ) from six to 12 nautical miles offshore, about 22.2 kilometres. A major reform meant to protect artisanal fishers has been passed, yet some of the people it is meant to protect have not heard of it. As Ghana marks World Fisheries Day, that gap deserves serious attention. The real test of the expanded IEZ is not how far the boundary extends on paper. It is whether fishers like Kwesi can go to sea knowing that their grounds are protected and that violations will not go unchecked. The stakes are high Fish provides roughly 60 per cent of the animal protein Ghanaians eat, according to the National Development Planning Commission’s 2024 Annual Progress Report. The artisanal subsector accounts for over 70 per cent of total fish production and supports an estimated three million people. Women dominate the post-harvest chain, processing, smoking and trading the catch. When catches fall, the damage does not stop at the beach. It affects processors, traders, transporters, canoe owners and consumers. Protecting artisanal fishing grounds is therefore not a concession to one group of resource users. It is an investment in food security and coastal economies. Pressure on fish stocks is also growing. Declining stocks, illegal fishing, unsustainable methods and competition for fishing grounds all threaten marine resources. Industrial bottom trawling is a particular concern when conducted irresponsibly or in violation of fisheries regulations: it can damage seabed habitats, catch non-target species and remove juvenile fish before they have reproduced. For artisanal fishers, the consequences are immediate: fewer fish, longer trips and reduced incomes. A boundary is not a guarantee Incursions into restricted waters are not new. Research has documented industrial trawlers entering them, particularly during upwelling seasons, when nutrient-rich waters boost fish abundance. Analysis of Vessel Monitoring System data from 2023 to 2024 found continued incursions, with repeated violations concentrated in particular locations and involving a subset of operators. Without adequate monitoring, clear communication and credible sanctions, the expanded protection may not translate into real improvements for artisanal fishers. Enforcement matters even more now that the expanded IEZ changes the area available to industrial operators. Kwesi says that had he and his fellow fishers known about the restrictions on industrial fishing within the IEZ, they would have been better equipped to identify and report suspected violations. Other community members echoed his concerns and called for sustained education on what the law provides, what is prohibited within the IEZ and how to report suspected infractions. Taking the IEZ From Paper to Practice First, fishers must know where the boundary is. Government must ensure that official maps and geographical coordinates of the expanded IEZ are published and widely disseminated, and incorporated into nautical charts, vessel navigation systems and monitoring platforms. Fishers must be able to tell when an industrial vessel is operating in restricted waters. A boundary that cannot be identified or monitored at sea will be difficult to enforce. It is important that the law be known, and reporting must work. The Fisheries Commission and other relevant institutions should intensify education on the Act in coastal communities, in accessible local languages and through channels fishers trust: community meetings, fisher associations, local radio, landing beach structures and traditional leadership networks. Fishers should know their rights, what industrial operators may not do, where to report suspected infractions, which institution receives complaints and what happens after a report is made. Lastly, enforcement must be credible. The Fisheries Commission and relevant enforcement agencies must strengthen the use of Vessel Monitoring Systems, surveillance and at-sea patrols, particularly where research has identified repeated violations. The institutions responsible for fisheries management, maritime surveillance and law enforcement must coordinate, and where violations are established, sanctions must follow. Fishers should be partners, not only beneficiaries: they hold valuable knowledge of fishing grounds, seasonal patterns and activity at sea, and should have a meaningful say in decisions about the resource they depend on. Beyond the Law Ghana has taken an important legislative step. What matters now is whether industrial vessels respect the new boundary, whether fishing communities understand and can use the protection it offers, and whether violations are detected and addressed. For Kwesi, the value of the expanded IEZ will not be measured by the additional six nautical miles alone. It will be measured by whether he and his fellow fishers can go to sea with greater security, face fewer incursions and return with catches that sustain their families. An exclusion zone that exists only on paper cannot protect a fisher’s livelihood. The task now is to make that protection real.

items.title: Trial of killers of Ademola, Salami begins in Lagos
items.description: By Innocent Anaba THE long-awaited trial of four persons accused of the alleged murder of Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sherriff Ishola Salami in the Ajiran area of Lagos State commenced yesterday, with the Lagos State prosecution opening its case before the court. The trial began before Justice A. Muyideen of the Lagos State High Court sitting in Igbosere.Those standing trial are Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo; Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga; Tajudeen Ahmed, aka Ahmed Ajiran; and Bode Ajose. The prosecution team was led by the Lagos State Solicitor-General, Mr Adebayo Haroon, while the defence counsel included Mr O. Ajanaku, Mr R. Owolabi, Mr Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and Mr Gbenga Ojo, who represented the third defendant. Mr M. Familola represented the fourth defendant. The prosecution called its first witness, ASP Nosiru Isiaka, a police officer attached to Special Squad 1 of the Lagos State Police Command, who testified on the circumstances surrounding the investigation and eventual arrest of the defendants. In his evidence-in-chief, ASP Isiaka narrated how the police initially arrested the first two suspects, Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo, and Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga, and how the third suspect was later arrested through the technical team from the Inspector-General of Police’s office in the Ajiran area of Ajah. He further told the court how investigations eventually led to the arrest of the third defendant. He was about to narrate how the investigation led to the arrest of the fourth suspect, Mr Ahmed Tajudeen, when his testimony was interrupted by the defence counsel. The police witness, while recounting the investigative steps taken by his team, explained how information obtained during the investigation helped the police establish links between the four defendants and the alleged murder of the two victims. However, proceedings were interrupted by objections from the defence counsel, Ojo, SAN, and the other three lawyers representing the defendants, who challenged the manner in which the prosecution witness was presenting his evidence. Ojo, who is the leading counsel to the defendants, argued that the police Investigating Police Officer (IPO), being the first prosecution witness, could not give evidence. in a manner suggesting that he personally witnessed the circumstances surrounding the killings when, in fact, he was only an investigating officer who was not present at the scene of the alleged crime. He maintained that the witness must confine his testimony to facts within his personal knowledge and properly distinguish between what he personally did or observed during the investigation and information allegedly obtained from other persons in the course of police inquiries. The objection interrupted the proceedings as the defence sought to ensure that the prosecution’s evidence remained within the boundaries of admissible evidence under the law. Further hearing in the matter has been adjourned until November 25. The post Trial of killers of Ademola, Salami begins in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le gouvernement oblige les bouchers à afficher les prix et à distinguer les viandes locales des viandes importées
items.description: Le gouvernement, représenté par les ministères de l’Intérieur, de l’Industrie et du Commerce, de l’Investissement économique, ainsi que de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, a adressé des instructions à ses services au niveau des préfectures et provinces afin d’obliger les vendeurs de viandes rouges à afficher les prix et à préciser l’origine des viandes, en distinguant les produits locaux des produits import20és. Selon une circulaire conjointe adressée aux walis et gouverneurs, aux délégués de l’Industrie et du Commerce, aux directeurs régionaux et provinciaux de l’Agriculture ainsi qu’aux responsables de l’Office national de sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires (ONSSA), les bouchers sont désormais tenus d’afficher les prix de vente et de préciser l’origine des viandes rouges, qu’elles soient locales ou importées. Cette mesure s’inscrit, selon les départements concernés, dans le cadre des opérations de veille et de suivi de la situation du marché national. Les services gouvernementaux ont en effet relevé certaines pratiques commerciales dans le secteur de la vente au détail des viandes rouges, notamment l’absence d’affichage détaillé des prix selon les catégories et l’origine des produits proposés à la vente. La circulaire souligne que ces pratiques ont contribué à « créer une confusion chez les consommateurs quant à la distinction, dans les boucheries et les points de vente au détail, entre les prix des viandes locales et ceux des viandes importées ou provenant de cheptels importés destinés à l’abattage ». Une situation qui constitue une infraction aux dispositions légales et réglementaires en vigueur, lesquelles obligent tout fournisseur à permettre au consommateur de connaître, outre les prix, les caractéristiques essentielles du produit, de la marchandise ou du service, et à lui fournir les informations nécessaires pour effectuer un choix éclairé en fonction de ses besoins et de ses moyens. La circulaire insiste ainsi sur la nécessité d’appliquer les dispositions de l’article 3 de la loi n° 31.08 édictant des mesures de protection du consommateur, ainsi que celles du décret n° 2.12.503 pris pour son application. Les propriétaires des boucheries et des points de vente de viandes rouges sont, à ce titre, tenus d’afficher les prix et de préciser l’origine des viandes de manière claire, transparente et lisible. Le document appelle également à distinguer les prix des viandes locales de ceux des viandes importées, ainsi que des viandes issues de cheptels importés destinés à l’abattage. Cette distinction doit être présentée de façon transparente et suffisamment visible pour les consommateurs. Les propriétaires des boucheries et des points de vente au détail sont par ailleurs appelés à indiquer le prix de chaque catégorie de viande, en apposant l’étiquette correspondante directement sur le produit ou à proximité de celui-ci. La circulaire conjointe impose également aux professionnels d’établir un lien explicite entre le prix et l’origine de la viande, afin de permettre aux consommateurs d'identifier clairement le tarif de chaque catégorie et sa provenance. Les fournisseurs doivent ainsi faire figurer ces deux informations sur une même affiche ou sur une étiquette placée à proximité du produit, conformément à l’article 3 de la loi n° 31.08 et aux dispositions relatives à l’information du consommateur. Le document instruit également les responsables concernés de « prendre les mesures nécessaires pour obliger les bouchers et les vendeurs de viandes rouges en gros (…) à faire figurer sur les factures et les bons de livraison attestant des ventes effectuées au profit des détaillants les informations relatives à la catégorie du cheptel dont proviennent les carcasses, les quartiers et les viandes, en précisant s’il est d’origine locale ou importé, ainsi que le pays d’origine pour les animaux importés, les quantités de viande et les prix de vente en gros selon chaque catégorie ». La circulaire précise en outre que « les services vétérinaires de l’Office national de sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires chargés du contrôle du cheptel destiné à l’abattage, des carcasses et des viandes préparées dans les abattoirs et destinées à la vente doivent prendre les mesures nécessaires pour apposer un cachet sur les carcasses et leurs parties, permettant de distinguer les viandes issues d’animaux d’origine locale de celles provenant de cheptels importés destinés à l’abattage ». S’agissant des viandes préparées, congelées ou réfrigérées, importées, le document indique que « les services de l’ONSSA chargés du contrôle au niveau des postes-frontières doivent veiller à la disponibilité des documents et des données obligatoires précisant l’origine et la nature de ces viandes, ainsi que des autres informations prévues par les dispositions légales et réglementaires en vigueur, et à l’apposition d’un cachet indiquant leur caractère importé ». Enfin, la circulaire insiste sur la nécessité de veiller au respect de ces mesures par les commerçants de viandes en gros et au détail ainsi que par les autres intervenants concernés. Elle prévoit également la programmation d’opérations de contrôle et le renforcement de leur fréquence au cours de la prochaine période, tout en appelant à appliquer les sanctions prévues par les lois et règlements en vigueur à l’encontre des contrevenants. items.title: Journée mondiale des toilettes : au Maroc, EWA appelle à créer 100 000 sanitaires publics d’ici 2030
items.description: À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale des toilettes, célébrée ce 19 novembre, Environment Women Association (EWA) appelle à faire de l’accès à des sanitaires publics propres, sûrs et accessibles une priorité nationale. L’association propose notamment d’étudier un objectif de 100 000 installations créées, réhabilitées ou remises à niveau à l’horizon 2030, dans la perspective notamment de la Coupe du monde. Au Maroc, la question des sanitaires publics entend sortir de l’angle mort du débat public. À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale des toilettes, Environment Women Association (EWA) clôture sa campagne de sensibilisation « 100 jours, 100 messages, un même combat : la dignité », lancée le 11 août dernier, par un appel à passer de la sensibilisation à l’action. L’association, présidée par Farida Jaïdi, défend l’idée que l’accès à des sanitaires propres, sûrs, accessibles et correctement entretenus constitue un enjeu de santé publique, d’égalité et de dignité. Au cœur de son plaidoyer figure une proposition : étudier la possibilité de créer, réhabiliter ou remettre à niveau 100 000 toilettes publiques d’ici 2030. EWA précise toutefois qu’il s’agit d’une ambition de plaidoyer qui n’a pas encore été adoptée officiellement par les pouvoirs publics. Une question de dignité et de santé publique Pour EWA, l’absence de sanitaires adaptés ou leur mauvais état ne constitue pas seulement un problème de confort. Elle peut avoir des conséquences sur la santé, l’hygiène, la sécurité et la mobilité des citoyens. Les femmes et les filles sont particulièrement concernées, notamment en raison des besoins liés à l’hygiène menstruelle. Les enfants, les personnes âgées et les personnes en situation de handicap peuvent également être confrontés à des difficultés lorsque les équipements sont inexistants ou inaccessibles. L’association estime ainsi que la question de l’assainissement public se situe au croisement de plusieurs enjeux : santé, égalité, éducation, sécurité, environnement et respect de la personne. L’échéance de 2030, année durant laquelle le Maroc accueillera la Coupe du monde avec l’Espagne et le Portugal, donne une dimension supplémentaire à cette réflexion. Pour EWA, l’amélioration des infrastructures ne devrait pas se limiter aux stades ou aux principaux sites fréquentés par les visiteurs. Les marchés, jardins, gares, pôles de transport, espaces de loisirs, quartiers et autres lieux publics devraient également être pris en compte. L’association estime que l’organisation du Mondial pourrait constituer une opportunité pour renforcer les infrastructures et améliorer la qualité des services proposés à la population comme aux visiteurs. 100 000 installations : une ambition à construire EWA propose ainsi d’engager dès maintenant une réflexion sur un objectif de 100 000 sanitaires publics à l’horizon 2030. Pour rendre cette ambition crédible, l’association préconise notamment de réaliser un état des lieux national des installations existantes, d’identifier les territoires prioritaires et d’intégrer les sanitaires publics aux projets d’aménagement et de rénovation des espaces collectifs. Elle appelle également à définir des critères minimaux portant sur l’accès à l’eau, l’hygiène, l’éclairage, la sécurité, l’intimité et l’accessibilité aux personnes en situation de handicap. La prise en compte des besoins spécifiques des femmes et des filles figure également parmi les priorités avancées. Mais au-delà de la construction, l’association insiste sur un autre enjeu : l’entretien. « Un sanitaire construit mais laissé à l’abandon ne répond pas durablement aux besoins des citoyens », souligne-t-elle, en appelant à considérer la maintenance comme une composante essentielle de toute politique d’assainissement public. Une responsabilité partagée La mise en œuvre d’une telle ambition nécessiterait une coordination entre les pouvoirs publics, les collectivités territoriales, les gestionnaires d’espaces collectifs, les entreprises, les associations et les citoyens. EWA rappelle néanmoins que la responsabilité doit rester clairement répartie. Les collectivités peuvent identifier les besoins locaux et agir sur les espaces relevant de leur compétence, tandis que les entreprises et gestionnaires d’équipements doivent assurer la qualité des installations placées sous leur responsabilité. De leur côté, les associations ont un rôle de sensibilisation et de mobilisation, tandis que les citoyens sont appelés à respecter les équipements et à signaler les dégradations. « La dignité ne se proclame pas seulement » Après cent jours de campagne, EWA souhaite désormais transformer son plaidoyer en débat public et encourager les acteurs concernés à examiner la faisabilité de son objectif. Pour l’association, la Journée mondiale des toilettes constitue ainsi bien davantage qu’un rendez-vous symbolique. Elle doit permettre de rappeler qu’un besoin aussi élémentaire que l’accès à des sanitaires dignes peut directement conditionner la santé, la mobilité, l’éducation et l’égalité. Avec la perspective de 2030, EWA entend donc placer la question des sanitaires publics parmi les enjeux d’infrastructure et de qualité de vie à prendre en compte dès aujourd’hui. items.title: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of ‘baseless slander’
items.description: Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk’s representatives of repeatedly asking a country football federation employee to “falsely” take the blame for the winger’s positive drugs test. Tottenham winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium. The 25-year-old said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty. In a Wednesday interview, Mudryk firmly placed the blame for his 20-month absence on his national association, prompting Shevchenko’s response. In a statement, former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko, who is now president of the UAF, said Mudryk’s comments amounted to a “baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally” and called on the player to retract his words. He added: “His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample. “The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.” He added that “numerous investigations and audits” undertaken as part of the case were unable to shed light on when or where the substance entered Mudryk’s system. In his interview Mudryk also claimed Shevchenko had offered him little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and said its handling of the matter delayed his return to football. However, Shevchenko went on to say that national team staff had complied with a request from Chelsea not to provide Mudryk with any medication while on international duty. And he also challenged the former Shakhtar Donetsk forward to provide evidence “to back up his words”. “Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps,” Shevchenko added. “These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine. “The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case. “I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. “If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.” BBC Sport has contacted Mudryk’s representatives for comment.

items.title: 11-Décembre 2026 : La parade militaire signe son retour sous le signe de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire
items.description: Le Burkina Faso s'apprête à célébrer sa Fête nationale du 11 décembre 2026 sous le signe de l'affirmation patriotique et de la mémoire historique. Lors du Conseil des ministres réuni sous la présidence du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, une communication orale a fixé le cap de cette édition organisée dans la capitale. Placée sous un thème axé sur la Révolution Progressiste Populaire et l'héritage des luttes anti-impérialistes, la célébration s'annonce inédite et sera rehaussée par une grande parade militaire. Les préparatifs de la commémoration de la Fête nationale sont officiellement lancés au plus haut niveau de l'État. Au cours de sa séance ordinaire du jeudi 19 novembre 2026, présidée par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Conseil des ministres a examiné les modalités d'organisation des festivités du 11 décembre prochain. Selon le ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, cette édition 2026 a été pensée pour marquer les esprits par son caractère solennel et rassembleur au cœur de la capitale. Le choix de la thématique retenue traduit la vision politique et doctrinale portée par les autorités de la Transition. L'édition 2026 est formellement placée sous le thème : « Révolution Progressiste Populaire au Burkina Faso : une consécration des résistances à la domination coloniale et à l’impérialisme ». À travers cet intitulé, le gouvernement entend relier l'engagement citoyen contemporain aux combats historiques menés par le peuple burkinabè pour sa dignité, son indépendance réelle et l'autodétermination de ses choix stratégiques. Sur le plan événementiel, le rassemblement national s'articulera autour de moments forts de démonstration patriotique. Les autorités ont annoncé une célébration inédite qui se tiendra à Ouagadougou, dont le clou sera une grande parade militaire regroupant les Forces d'armées, les Forces de sécurité intérieure et les composantes engagées dans la défense du territoire. Cette manifestation populaire visera à réaffirmer la cohésion nationale, l'unité entre le peuple et ses forces combattantes, ainsi que la détermination de la Nation à poursuivre sa marche vers la souveraineté. items.title: GRA rejects claims lifestyle audits are overreach to meet tax targets
items.description: Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) Commissioner-General Anthony Kwasi Sarpong has rejected the suggestion that the authority is resorting to lifestyle audits and other compliance measures because it is under pressure to meet revenue targets. Asked whether the approach risked overreaching taxpayers, he replied: “Not at all.” Mr Sarpong told host George Wiafe on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday that the measures were part of efforts to address Ghana’s low tax-to-GDP ratio and close leakages in the system. He did not detail how lifestyle audits are conducted. He described how the GRA can use taxpayers’ own information to assess their tax obligations. “When we invite the taxpayers and show them their own data,” he said, officers can compare a person’s tax return with information on vehicles acquired and goods imported. “When you put it all together, this is what we believe your income should be, and this is the tax you should pay.” The GRA boss said Ghana’s tax-to-GDP ratio was below the African average, which he put at about 16%. He argued that the gap showed tax collection was not keeping pace with economic activity. “That means that there are leakages in the system,” he said. Mr Sarpong cited a 2027 projection of 17.9%, almost 18%, saying compliance measures and structural reforms were expected to help block those leakages. He said the government was supporting the GRA to address gaps linked to unavailable systems and a lack of investment.

items.title: Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm
items.description: By Matthew Johnson The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional. Vice-President of SOFPON, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, who disclosed this during a press conference themed, “Primary Health Care Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?”, will also focus on “The Double Burden of Disease and the Cost of Fragmented Care” and “The Stressed Family Physician and Continuity of Care”. on November 19th 2026 ahead of the society’s 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting ,AGSM, said the country’s primary healthcare system was facing a serious operational crisis. He explained that the shortage of skilled medical personnel, poor funding and increasing migration of doctors were undermining access to quality healthcare, calling on the Federal Government and state governors to urgently integrate family physicians into the leadership of primary healthcare facilities. Yakubu who said the majority of PHCs were unable to provide essential medical services due to structural decay, inadequate funding and shortage of skilled health professionals. According to him, the conference will develop policy and clinical recommendations on integrating specialist services into primary healthcare, improving physician welfare and retention, and developing integrated care models for infectious and chronic diseases. He described the situation was being worsened by the increasing migration of doctors, particularly frontline medical professionals, due to poor working conditions, inadequate equipment and weak welfare structures. He said loss or sidelining of family physicians could further weaken the country’s healthcare delivery system, particularly at the grassroots where continuous and comprehensive medical care is required. He further explained that family physicians were specially trained to manage patients holistically, coordinate treatment and address both infectious and chronic diseases at the primary healthcare level. Yakubu said the country’s healthcare system was battling a double burden of disease, with communicable illnesses such as malaria, tuberculosis and cholera existing alongside rising cases of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, kidney diseases and cancer. He warned that the absence of coordinated healthcare services was increasing treatment costs for families and making it difficult to manage patients with multiple health conditions. He said the society also urged governments to move beyond constructing PHC buildings to adequately equipping existing facilities and providing sufficient funding and personnel to operate them. Yakubu added that positioning family physicians at the centre of primary healthcare would promote early detection of chronic illnesses, reduce treatment costs and ensure continuity of care. He said: “Data shows that only about 20 per cent of the over 30,000 PHC facilities across Nigeria are fully functional, with a vast majority unable to provide essential medical services. “The rest suffer from structural decay, severe funding deficits that fall far below the 15 per cent Abuja Declaration target, and a devastating shortage of skilled medical professionals. “When you remove the Family Physician, the specialist trained specifically to manage multi-dimensional, continuous, and holistic patient care from the community level, you create an unfillable gap. “We are here today to tell the government and the public that Nigeria cannot afford this gap. Fragmented care is too expensive, too dangerous, and completely unsustainable,” he said. “The society also raised concerns over the welfare of doctors, warning that excessive patient workloads, burnout, economic pressures and security threats were affecting the quality and continuity of healthcare delivery. A single family doctor in Nigeria today routinely consults for numbers of patients that far exceed international safety standards. “Why does the stress of a doctor matter to the average Nigerian citizen? It matters because a stressed doctor is a direct threat to the continuity of care. If we want a healthy nation, we must care for the people who care for the sick. A broken doctor cannot heal a broken healthcare system. “Against this backdrop, SOFPON called on the Federal Ministry of Health, state governors and health sector administrators to make the integration of certified family physicians into the administrative and clinical leadership of primary healthcare authorities mandatory. “I further called for targeted rural allowances and improved security measures for doctors working in underserved and high-risk communities.” Yakubu said. SOFPON said the issues would form part of discussions at the 29th AGSM, where family physicians, medical scholars and policymakers would examine strategies for strengthening primary healthcare delivery. The post Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le gouvernement annonce la reprise de l’exploitation de la mine de zinc de Perkoa
items.description: Le gouvernement burkinabè franchit un cap décisif dans la redynamisation de son secteur minier et le développement économique régional. Réuni en Conseil des ministres sous la présidence du Chef de l'État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, l'exécutif a adopté un décret accordant le permis d’exploitation industrielle de grande mine de zinc à la société SOPAMIB Perkoa SA, dans la commune de Réo. Entre la perspective d'injections financières majeures dans les caisses publiques et la création de plus de 1 200 emplois, cette décision marque le redémarrage tant attendu d’un site extractif stratégique. Le secteur extractif burkinabè enregistre le retour aux affaires d’un de ses fleurons industriels. Au titre du ministère de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Conseil des ministres du jeudi 19 novembre 2026 a entériné l'octroi du permis d'exploitation industrielle de grande mine de zinc à la société SOPAMIB Perkoa SA. Situé dans la commune de Réo, province du Sanguié (région de Nando), ce projet extractif bénéficie désormais d’un cadre juridique renouvelé pour redémarrer ses opérations. Selon le ministre chargé du portefeuille minier, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette réattribution vise directement à relancer la production minière à l'échelle régionale et à valoriser les ressources sous-terraines de la Nation. Au-delà de l'enjeu industriel, la relance du gisement de Perkoa constitue une opération budgétaire de premier ordre. Les projections officielles présentées par le gouvernement indiquent que la mise en service et l'exploitation continue de cette grande mine de zinc généreront un peu plus de 96 milliards de francs CFA au profit direct du budget de l'État. Dans un contexte d'effort national de mobilisation des ressources intérieures, cette contribution financière substantielle vient consolider les capacités d'investissement de la puissance publique. Sur le plan social, le redémarrage du site de Perkoa apporte une réponse concrète aux attentes d'insertion professionnelle des jeunes. Les données du ministère des Mines prévoient la création immédiate de 400 emplois directs et de 850 emplois indirects à travers les sous-traitances et les services associés. Cette impulsion socio-économique devrait stimuler le commerce de proximité, renforcer les infrastructures de la commune de Réo et offrir de nouvelles perspectives de revenus aux communautés hôtes de la région de Nando. items.title: The Limits of Positive Thinking
items.description: A s anxious Americans dealt with a cascade of computer failures over the past week, Donald Trump offered this advice: “Relax.” The air-traffic-control system, email providers, banks, airlines, and even the internal communications system of the country’s biggest intelligence agency had all seen outages, fueling fears of digital conspiracy. But they weren’t connected, the president assured Fox News. And hackers were not behind the outages, he insisted, because no one would dare risk retaliation by the United States. Companies were simply replacing outdated equipment, “and things happen when you put in new equipment,” he said. There was nothing to see here, no cause for alarm. “Everything’s good.” Digital-security experts are not nearly so sanguine. They see something new and potentially ominous that’s fueling these hugely disruptive outages: artificial intelligence. Companies haven’t been replacing old equipment so much as rapidly patching newly discovered flaws in their systems with the help of sophisticated AI that can quickly spot vulnerabilities. And why are companies moving so fast? Because attackers have AI too. The FBI warned this week about an AI-enabled tool set, called ARTEX, that “cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers” are using to identify weakness and develop attacks in under three hours. None of the affected companies has said that it thinks its systems went down because of an attack. But security experts told us that in the past few weeks, they have been struggling to keep up with an onslaught of attempted hacks from AI-enabled adversaries. And rushing to harden lots of computer infrastructure all at once can be messy and inconsistent, explaining some of the disruptions. Trump has never fully reckoned with the risks of AI. He prefers to call it “superintelligence,” an odd choice given that that’s the term some doomsayers use for AI that becomes self-aware and tries to wipe out humanity. The president frames the race to develop advanced AI as an existential contest between China and the United States. “Whoever wins AI wins,” he is fond of saying. The Defense Department has deployed AI systems across its networks with seemingly little regard for the risks of using them in combat. Trump has avoided creating safety regulations and guardrails and has followed the counsel of executives whose fortunes depend on AI expansion. That includes ex–Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has consistently downplayed the risk of out-of-control AI, calling apocalyptic scenarios “made-up” or baseless. When it comes to developing and deploying the technology, Trump is all gas and no brakes. For a different president, the nerve-racking outages of the past week might have been a moment for sober reflection on whether the United States is prepared for what’s coming. Even some Republicans are asking for that, as are some Democrats. “It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” Senator Mark Warner of Virginia, a Democrat who is in line to chair the Senate Intelligence Committee in the next Congress, said in a statement. Warner has proposed legislation that would subject AI models to greater scrutiny and safety checks. “Americans deserve clear, reliable information and a government that is prepared to respond,” Warner said. But the administration seems not to grasp how worried many Americans are at suddenly being unable to check their bank balance or read their email. The disappearance of everyday conveniences comes after months of dark warnings about rogue AI agents and renewed fears of cyberattacks from Iran. The French government publicly accused Iran last week of remotely sabotaging food-refrigeration units and causing mass spoilage in grocery stores. Trump may insist that there’s nothing to be concerned about, but even some of his allies fear that something bigger is at play. “If this is all a coincidence,” Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri, a Republican, told reporters on Tuesday, “it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.” N ormally, in the middle of a domestic crisis, an administration tries to speak with one voice and tell a coherent story to an anxious public. But as bank websites crashed at the same time as stranded passengers slept in airports, no one in the administration seemed to know what was happening or who was in charge of fixing things. On Monday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who is supposed to lead the government’s response to domestic cybersecurity incidents, suggested that artificial intelligence deployed on computer networks was “self-fixing itself.” In the scenario he described, recent network collapses were the result of a big, messy patching job. That is close to what experts think is continuing to happen. But Mullin attributed his understanding to a tech leader, whom he declined to name, telling Fox News that his theory “kind of makes sense.” This uncertain description, from an official with access to an array of classified government intelligence and seasoned briefers, did little to allay concerns. [ Read: The secretary of imprecision ] The unit within Mullin’s department that should be running point in this crisis, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency , has lost almost a third of its 3,200 employees since Trump returned to office two years ago. The White House wants to cut the budget for some agency programs, including election security, by $700 million next year. When we went to the CISA website today, we found guidance about recent incidents, forms for reporting cyberattacks, and a two-month-old handbook for “Communicating Under Pressure.” “During service outages, clear communication matters,” CISA unironically advised. Officials dismissed any connection between the computer failures and the deep staffing and budget cuts at the agency. “The implication that the recent events would not have occurred if CISA had more employees is patently false,” a White House official said. The new director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, told a congressional committee yesterday that “the timing of these ​incidents can raise questions, ​and it should,” but he insisted that the outages were coincidental and “associated with maintenance and ​technical ​changes.” Clayton also blamed the patching of vulnerabilities, but he didn’t blame AI. Marco Rubio , the secretary of state and the national security adviser, appeared initially confused when a reporter asked at a press conference in Manila whether AI had played a role in the outages. He said he couldn’t confirm that that was the case but explained why AI hypothetically could have led to the systems failing. Rubio stressed that “people are fearful; people are uncertain” and said that it was important for the administration to “share with them transparently what we know.” T rump’s habit, when he is confronted with a crisis, is to rely on the power of positive thinking. In the first weeks of 2020, he was slow to sound the alarm on a new virus discovered in China, reportedly for fear of rattling financial markets and upsetting Xi Jinping. By the time he left office a year later, some 400,000 people in the United States had died of COVID-19 . A similar dynamic now seems to be at work. Trump has resisted calls even from within the AI industry to regulate the technology, fearing that government interference will stymie innovation and slow growth. The president knows that AI companies are propping up the stock market and that U.S. economic expansion depends largely on the construction of new data centers, which are essential for developing more powerful AI models. Trump was in China this week for meetings with Xi and Vladimir Putin, and he indicated to allies that he didn’t want anything to distract from those sessions. That could explain the at-times-nonexistent messaging from the White House. During the height of Friday’s ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration—which does not appear to have been caused by AI-related patching—Trump was huddled in the Oval Office with the actor Jon Voight, talking about Hollywood tax rebates. He stayed out of sight for days, leaving Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to make a widely panned series of appearances in which they largely blamed the Biden administration and demanded money from Congress. One air traffic controller told us that everything he and his colleagues had learned about the nationwide ground stop—an event that has happened only three times this century—came from the same general announcement Duffy had made to the public. The controller said that he had received no information internally about the outage and its causes. Officials privately acknowledge that an extraordinary amount of work needs to be done to fend off the relentless and increasing AI attacks. But the president’s advisers may be wary of telling the public the truth about the scale of the threat because they don’t want to make Trump angry, two Republicans close to the White House told us on the condition of anonymity to discuss private conversations. [ Read: Trump sets the olive branch on fire ] In his Fox News interview, Trump said that journalists were exploiting the computer crashes for political purposes: “The press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would’ve happened two years ago, three years ago, in the Biden administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would’ve mentioned it.” Journalists extensively covered similar breakdowns, including a nationwide ground stop in 2023 and the discovery of a massive penetration of U.S. telecom networks by China, through an actor known as Salt Typhoon, the following year. Trump insisted on Fox News that the weeklong parade of cyber horribles was a mere coincidence. “I’ll let you know if there’s a problem,” he said. After the past week, the bar for what Trump considers to be a problem is looking awfully high. Isaac Stanley-Becker and Madison Hahamy contributed to this article.

The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM). “The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay. The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said. It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos. “Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying. “By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added. Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said, “We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.” The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support. CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts in Lagos. Organised by Afreximbank, hosted by the Government of Nigeria and delivered in partnership with the African Union Commission and the AfCFTA Secretariat, it brought together creatives, investors, buyers and policymakers from Africa, the Caribbean and the diaspora. NEXIM is Nigeria’s export credit agency and is owned equally by the Ministry of Finance Incorporated and the Central Bank of Nigeria. items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Un greffier écroué pour une affaire d’escroquerie de 4,5 millions FCFA autour d’une fausse vente aux enchères
items.description: Un greffier en service au Tribunal du travail de Bobo-Dioulasso est poursuivi pour des faits présumés d’escroquerie et d’abus de fonction. Il lui est reproché d’avoir encaissé 4,5 millions de FCFA auprès d’un particulier en lui promettant trois véhicules dans le cadre d’une prétendue vente aux enchères de la Cour d’appel. Une affaire présumée d’escroquerie impliquant un auxiliaire de justice est entre les mains du parquet de Bobo-Dioulasso. Un greffier en fonction au Tribunal du travail de la ville est poursuivi pour avoir prétendument organisé une fausse opération de vente aux enchères de véhicules, qui lui aurait permis d’obtenir 4,5 millions de FCFA auprès d’un particulier. Selon un communiqué du Procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso, les faits remontent à mai 2026. Le mis en cause aurait proposé à un particulier d’acquérir trois véhicules présentés comme faisant partie d’une vente aux enchères qui devait être organisée par la Cour d’appel de Bobo-Dioulasso. Convaincu de la réalité de l’opération, le particulier aurait remis au greffier la somme de 4,5 millions de FCFA en vue de concrétiser cette acquisition. Mais la vente annoncée n’a finalement jamais eu lieu. Le plaignant aurait alors découvert que l’opération était fictive et qu’elle aurait été montée dans le but de lui soutirer de l’argent. Le greffier placé sous mandat de dépôt À la suite de la plainte, le parquet a diligenté une enquête pour faire la lumière sur cette affaire. Au terme des investigations, le greffier a été poursuivi pour des faits présumés d’escroquerie et d’abus de fonction, sur la base des articles 332-12, 613-1 et 613-2 du Code pénal. Il a ensuite été placé sous mandat de dépôt, dans l’attente de la suite de la procédure judiciaire. Le parquet appelle les éventuelles victimes à se manifester Dans son communiqué daté du 18 novembre 2026, le Procureur du Faso, Sékou Traoré, réaffirme la détermination du parquet à lutter contre toutes les formes de délinquance et à veiller au respect de la loi. Il invite par ailleurs toute personne disposant d’informations sur de telles pratiques, ou estimant avoir été victime de faits similaires, à saisir son parquet afin de contribuer à la manifestation de la vérité. items.title: Black Challenge make history with Egypt win to reach Amputee World Cup semi-finals
items.description: Ghana’s Black Challenge have made history by beating Egypt 2-0 to reach the semi-finals of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The victory secures Ghana’s first-ever appearance in the last four of the competition, surpassing their previous best finish of sixth place. The Black Challenge faced a stubborn Egyptian side that adopted a defensive approach, sitting deep and frustrating the Ghanaians in the first half. However, forward Mubarik Mohammed proved decisive after the break, scoring twice to take his tournament tally to six goals and seal a historic victory for Ghana. The Black Challenge protected their lead until the final whistle to confirm their place in the semi-finals and record their best-ever finish at the tournament.

items.title: Korea sees Nigeria as gateway for K-Beauty in Africa – Deputy Head of Mission, Tak Namgung
items.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom Tak Namgung is the Deputy Head of Mission at the Korean Embassy in Abuja. He spoke to journalists on the sidelines of the Korea-Nigeria joint seminar at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos. Let us start with K-beauty. Your Ambassador spoke briefly about collaboration in that field. He said in the short term, K-beauty in Nigeria will mainly be about trade. What does that mean in practice? In the short term, it is about trade and expanding the market here in Nigeria. I recently spoke with fellow Korean diplomats who came to Lagos a month ago. They are based in Gabon, Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire. We share the same goal of promoting Korean beauty products. They told me they have a very strong chain — those trading in Gabon also have a network in Côte d’Ivoire, and a very strong branch in France. They are all connected. As some of you mentioned, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is important. When we see its full implementation, Nigeria will be a bridge, a gateway for all products. After speaking with my colleagues, I felt I must work harder to have a stronger market presence here in Nigeria, because they see more productivity and more profit in our neighbouring, front-running countries. That is what the Korean Embassy is doing right now. We know consumers deserve genuine products, without counterfeits. Proper registration will help them rely on local distributors. There are strong online customers. They are the ones in desperate need, so that they can have strong confidence in great products. And that opens the way for Korean manufacturers to come to Nigeria for production. The Ambassador also spoke about shea butter. How does that fit in? We spoke quite a lot about shea nuts. About 40 per cent of all shea nuts are produced here in Nigeria, but only about 1 per cent of the global shea market actually comes to Nigeria. Nigeria is heading to fill that gap. NIIA serves as a wonderful platform for such conversations. It provides the intellectual discourse between the Korean Embassy, the Korean government, and Nigerian authorities that will eventually contribute to policy, and also to the business side, for Korean business persons to come. There is a good example. As was said during the presentation, we will have Beauty West Africa in Lagos. There will be a Korean pavilion, and we will present K-beauty products. What would Korea gain from this collaboration? Today we held a seminar on cultural cooperation, in collaboration with NIIA. From here, we navigated the possible cultural collaboration. According to the data, Nigeria’s creative economy accounts for about 2.3 per cent of the GDP. Nigeria also expects, by 2030, to create 2 million jobs from the creative economy. So it gives more opportunities for Korea as well. Korea and Nigeria already have strong collaboration. For instance, we have had two joint dramas. One in 2024, titled My Sunshine, and this year, we also have My Alien Lover. That is the outcome of the collaboration between Korea and Nigeria. It is in Korean, English and Yoruba. So it shows a clear example of how our cultural collaboration is well maintained. Can you tell us about Korea’s cultural success and what Nigeria can learn from it? I would say Korea and Nigeria both have their unique cultures. It is about how both countries can have the opportunity to see each other. I am not saying this as a matter of capability or something. It is just a matter of time for Nigeria to flourish when it comes to cultural expansion. But what I would like to point out is that we need collaboration. With its unique culture, Korea also has some platforms to make use of. And Nigeria has the core culture that needs to be promoted across the world. What key steps is the Korean government taking to strengthen its cultural relationship with Nigeria? I would like to highlight K-beauty as one of the potential collaboration points. This November, we will have a K-beauty showcase and conference here in Lagos. And in two weeks, we will also have Beauty West Africa, also held in Lagos. We will have a Korean pavilion. So this is the first step we would like to take for Nigerians to enjoy Korean beauty products. But we also look forward to future collaboration in the near future because Nigeria has a large share in shea nut production. I also see it as an opportunity for potential collaboration in the field of cosmetics industry. One of the presenters mentioned cultural exchange between Korean and Nigerian artists. Is this something you are looking at? Yes. Fortunately, we do have a platform in place. We have the Korea Cultural Centre Nigeria, which was established in 2010. Now it is 2026, so it has been working for 16, 17 years. We also have the Korean scholarship programme, which brings an average of 10 Nigerian university students and others to Korea. And we also have the KOICA scholarship programme. KOICA is Korea’s development agency. We also have scholarships through it. With that human exchange, we expect — and the main point is — that they do not stay in Korea after graduation. They come back to Nigeria, and with affection for Korea, they come back to Nigeria and they become at the forefront in promoting cultural collaboration between the two countries. There is a Korean cultural centre here in Abuja. Is there a Nigerian art/cultural centre in Korea? Is it possible to have one, just like we have one here? I don’t think there is. It is at the discretion of the Nigerian authorities. But I think at least the conditions are already in place. Having an institution is important, but I would say the ambition I see here in Nigeria and also in Korea is already well in place. For instance, as I said during my speech, we recently had in Seoul the Seoul Africa Festival. There was a Nigerian performer who has been inspired by both Korean and Nigerian culture. He had a mixture of K-pop and Afrobeats. So, it also shows a clear example of how our culture can be assimilated and appeal to the general public in the world. The post Korea sees Nigeria as gateway for K-Beauty in Africa – Deputy Head of Mission, Tak Namgung appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Alibaba defrauded shareholders by concealing ties to suspected spy in Nvidia scandal, lawsuit says
items.description: Alibaba was sued on Thursday in New York by shareholders who accused the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week. According to a proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating, in its 2024, 2025, and 2026 annual reports, the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business. Shareholders cited Alibaba’s relationship with Megaspeed, a ​Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang ​had a relationship with Jensen Huang, who is not related to her. Shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week after media reports highlighted Alibaba’s ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had become Megaspeed’s “dominant” customer. They attributed part of the decline to a November 12 Reuters article saying Nvidia’s spy scandal could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on Chinese AI companies’ remote use of advanced processors. Alibaba did not immediately respond ‌to ⁠requests for comment. Eddie Wu, its chief executive, is also a defendant. Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations that its directors exercised lax oversight. Wu said on Thursday that Alibaba remained on track for $100 billion in external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin by 2030, despite US curbs on access to computing power that could affect the company’s products and services next year. The restrictions followed Huang’s resignation from Nvidia. In June, Alibaba sued the US government over being added to a blacklist of “Chinese ​military companies” that the Department of Defense linked to that country’s military. Last ​month, a federal ⁠judge in California granted Alibaba an injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon contracts to companies whose lobbyists also work with designated Chinese military companies. Alibaba said that restriction caused its lobbyists to retreat because they feared ⁠losing ​other clients, and violated its First Amendment constitutional right to speak ​to and petition the government. Thursday’s lawsuit by Alibaba shareholder Withida Bihan seeks unspecified damages for holders of Alibaba’s American depositary shares ​between May 23, 2024 and November 11, 2026.

items.title: ‘We shall win to sell Ghana’ – NDC MP gives NPP anthem a parliamentary remix
items.description: The familiar refrain of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) campaign anthem took an unexpected turn in Parliament when Chiana-Paga MP Alamzy Billa Nikyema gave it a provocative twist, drawing angry protests from the Minority leadership. In a light-hearted but politically charged intervention, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) MP recast the party’s familiar “We shall win to save Ghana ” refrain as “We shall win to sell Ghana”, prompting the Minority to demand that his remarks be expunged from the parliamentary record. The exchange turned a familiar political anthem into a fresh source of parliamentary friction, with the NDC MP’s satirical version drawing a sharp response from the very side whose song he had reworked. Mr Nikyema made the remark while accusing the NPP of obstructing efforts to fight illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, during its time in opposition. He recalled an earlier protest by NPP MPs, claiming that the party’s members had sat on the floor and sung the party anthem. But in his recollection, the lyrics had a different meaning. “When we tried fighting galamsey, you (NPP) were the same people who went and sat on the ground, and you were singing. If I got you right that time, you said, ‘We shall win to sell Ghana, we shall win to sell Ghana, the elephant is a stealing symbol, we shall win, to sell Ghana’,” he told the House. He insisted that he was merely repeating what he had heard during the protest. “Mr Speaker, I want to tell them that when they were singing, that is what I heard. Mr Speaker, I’m trying to say that when they were singing that very day, that is what I heard, and that is what my ears told me,” he added. The remark did not go down well with the Minority. The First Deputy Minority Whip, Habib Iddrisu, immediately rose to demand that the statement be removed from the official record, insisting that there was no such thing as the NPP singing that it would win to sell Ghana. “So, Mr Speaker, expunge that from the record. It should be expunged from the record,” he protested. Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin also urged the Speaker not to treat the matter lightly, arguing that the remark had no factual basis and required the Chair’s intervention. “Mr Speaker, let that be expunged from the record. What he said must be expunged from the record. There is no such factual basis for what he just said,” he insisted. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the MP should either withdraw the remark or have it removed from the record, warning that the Minority would take note of how the Chair handled the complaint.

items.title: Businessman remanded over alleged vehicle theft
items.description: An Accra Circuit Court has remanded a 39-year-old businessman into police custody for allegedly selling two vehicles worth GH¢380,000 and failing to account for the proceeds. Joseph Mbournyi pleaded not guilty to stealing and is expected to reappear before the court on November 23, 2026. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Emmanuel Nyamekye told Circuit Court 11 that the complainant, Mr Confidence Nyarko, an importer living at Ofankor, entrusted an unregistered 2020 Mitsubishi Outlander valued at GH¢250,000 to the accused for sale in October 2025. A witness also entrusted Mbournyi with an unregistered 2015 Toyota Vitz valued at GH¢130,000. The prosecution said Mbournyi, who resides at Ablekuma Odumase Adekorpa, took the vehicles to his garage at Achimota Christian Village and later requested their documents, claiming a bank was interested in purchasing them. The owners subsequently sent the documents via WhatsApp. According to the prosecution, Mbournyi sold the vehicles to different buyers but failed to remit the proceeds. During investigations, he allegedly admitted to selling the vehicles, using the money for personal purposes, and later asked for time to refund the amount.

items.title: Africa must be co-investor, not aid recipient, in proposed GECF gas bank — Expert
items.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said. Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call at the conclusion of the Eighth Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, while assessing key directions of Russian-African energy cooperation. Assessing the initiative to create a gas bank, Ikoneu described it as very good, but warned that its success would depend directly on a balance of interests. “It is important that this does not become just another multilateral investment institution where Africa’s interests are not put first,” she said. According to her, African countries should act not merely as recipients of funds, but as co-investors and full participants in strategic decision-making. Ikoneu said the bank should not only finance export infrastructure, but also the continent’s domestic needs, including electrification, petrochemicals, fertilizer production and industrial development, even given that many such projects are traditionally considered non-bankable. For the new structure to work effectively, she said it would need transparency, protection from political interference and coordination with the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and Africa Finance Corporation. She stressed that the continent’s domestic needs are extremely acute despite its wealth of energy resources with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without access to electricity. In this context, she said the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline — a project long stalled due to financing problems — takes on particular significance. Ikoenu noted that launching it requires a strong institutional framework among Nigeria, Niger and Algeria. At the same time, the pipeline should serve not only as an export channel to Europe but also as a driver of industrialisation for the participating countries. This, according to her, applies especially to Niger, which is critically dependent on imported electricity and costly diesel generators. An infrastructure union, she said, will allow the three countries to collectively defend their interests on the export market, while giving Russia the opportunity to act as a strategic partner both in the construction itself and in training the necessary personnel. Touching on the principle of technological neutrality enshrined in the GECF Moscow Declaration, the expert called for interpreting it as broadly as possible. “This should mean not just a choice between imported technologies, but also the freedom to develop one’s own,” she said. Ikoneu proposed creating a joint Russian-African research and innovation centre in the gas sector, expanding scholarship programmes for African students in Russia, and more actively involving women in the energy sector. The main priority, she said, is investment in African specialists and institutions capable of building their own industrial competencies. She emphasised the crucial role of the GECF as a platform for South-South cooperation among developing countries, saying that the Forum gives gas producers the opportunity to coordinate actions, ensure market transparency and shape fair pricing through long-term contracts. “A fair global gas market is not only one that guarantees supplies to consumers, but also one where resource-owning countries have a fair opportunity to benefit from them,” she explained. She warned that the value of such collective action by developing countries is especially high against the backdrop of current geopolitics. As the expert warned, “sanctions against one country can hit commercial agreements with another state that is not involved in the sanctions confrontation at all,” she said. items.title: La Cour d’appel de Tunis rend son verdict dans l’affaire Lourimi & Gharbi
items.description: La chambre criminelle spécialisée dans les affaires de terrorisme près la Cour d'appel de Tunis a rendu son verdict dans l'affaire visant Ajmi Lourimi et Mossaâb Gharbi. La justice a décidé de confirmer le verdict rendu le 3 juillet 2026 en première instance condamnant le secrétaire général d'Ennahdha Ajmi Lourimi et le militant du même parti, Mossaâb Gharbi, à trois ans de prisonn affirme Mosaïque FM, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, en citant une source proche du dossier. Cette affaire remonte à l'année 2024, lorsque les agents de la brigade de recherches et d'investigations de la Garde nationale de Tebourba ont procédé à l'arrestation d'Ajmi Lourimi. Ce dernier avait été interpellé à bord d'un véhicule dans la région de Borj El Amri, en compagnie d'un militant du mouvement Ennahdha faisant alors l'objet d'un avis de recherche au profit du Pôle judiciaire de lutte contre le terrorisme. Pour rappel Ajmi Lourimi est poursuivi pour « non-dénonciation aux autorités compétentes d'informations parvenues à sa connaissance concernant un crime terroriste » alors que Mossaâb Gharbi est accusé d'avoir fourni un lieu d'hébergement à une personne en lien avec des crimes terroristes et de l'avoir aidé à fuir. Y. N. L’article La Cour d’appel de Tunis rend son verdict dans l'affaire Lourimi & Gharbi est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: NDC celebrates National Chairman Zuwoghe on birthday
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has congratulated its National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, on his birthday, crediting him with steering the party’s growth into a national political platform within a few months of its establishment. In a birthday statement issued on Thursday and signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party praised Zuwoghe’s leadership, describing it as characterised by wisdom, maturity and political dexterity. The NDC said his leadership had transformed the party into a national brand, which it described as one of the fastest-growing opposition parties in Africa. The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) extends warm birthday wishes and heartfelt felicitations to our indefatigable National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe. “In just a few months of its establishment, he has steered the ship of the NDC with wisdom, maturity, and uncommon political dexterity, transforming it into a national brand that is the envy of many — indeed, the biggest, strongest, and fastest-growing opposition party in Africa.” The party further described the NDC as a “political Noah’s Ark” and a safe harbour for Nigerians seeking an alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). It said: “He has made the NDC a political Noah’s Ark, a safe harbour for all patriots that will rescue Nigeria from the buccaneering government of the ruling and ruinous APC.” The party wished the chairman long life, good health, greater wisdom, strength and prosperity, expressing hope that he would witness what it described as a new Nigeria under the NDC. It concluded: “Happy Birthday, Mr. Chairman! Happy Birthday, our Leader! Happy Birthday, our Captain!” The post NDC celebrates National Chairman Zuwoghe on birthday appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest
items.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo LOKOJA—THE Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims from a kidnappers’ den in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle between security operatives and the abductors. The victims, comprising men, women and children, were rescued in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-led joint security operation involving the police, military, forest guards and local security outfits. The Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Thursday while briefing journalists at the Police Headquarters in Lokoja. Bello Kankarofi said the operation was carried out following his directive, adding that the joint security team stormed the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. According to him, the superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some of them sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries. He said: “During the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.” The rescued victims were identified as Okuma Terlum, 47; Ojo Deborah, 23; Samuel Danjuma, three; Faith Raphael, 21; Emmanuella Raphael, three; Donald Tor, 31; Joseph Jonathan, 20; Tergu Joseph, 15; Samuel Joseph, eight; Engr. Joseph Adebija, 58; Lois Abiodun, 50; Chuks Obiakor, 45; Ola Olufemi, 58; Ankpe Godwin, 23; and Kuhwa Solomon, 25. The police commissioner disclosed that two other female victims, identified simply as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter in which the victims were kidnapped. He further revealed that the security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang while conveying the rescued victims out of the forest. “However, the operatives successfully repelled the attack and brought all 15 victims out safely.” The victims, who reportedly endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity, were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention. Although no arrests had been made as of the time of the briefing, the commissioner said actionable intelligence had been generated, while investigations were ongoing to track down the fleeing kidnappers and identify their sponsors. The post Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest appeared first on Vanguard News .
